A_general.open_code_note: The public repository contains client-side plugins, skills, and a CLI that connects to Learn MCP; it does not contain the hosted server implementation. Microsoft describes the hosted service as a remote server backed by Learn's knowledge service.
A_general.implementation_language: Hosted server: C# (official engineering blog); public client repository also contains TypeScript CLI code.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: Hosted server: official C# MCP SDK, version NOT FOUND. CLI dependency: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.27.1.
A_general.license: N/A for closed hosted server; CLI package is MIT licensed.
A_general.release_status: GA; release notes state general availability on 2025-11-07.
other_official_servers: https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp/openai-compatible — repository describes this as an experimental OpenAI-compatible endpoint for Deep Research models; it is a separate endpoint and not included in this server's actions.

Supplied OAuth metadata: origin /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource = HTTP 404; origin plus /api/mcp path = HTTP 404; /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server = HTTP 404. No authorization-server metadata or scopes were supplied.

No OAuth scopes, registration endpoint, grant types, PKCE, token methods, lifetime, or revocation data were returned.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. All three documented tools search or retrieve content; no write or destructive tool is listed. Tool annotations are not published in the reviewed sources. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented; the tools are read/retrieval operations. 3. Microsoft documents unauthenticated public access; no product-role inheritance or scopes are described. 4. The documented maxTokenBudget URL parameter limits search responses; fetch returns a full page. The FAQ says MCP does not provide filtering. An experimental OpenAI-compatible endpoint is separately documented. 5. The service is described as containing public documentation, not training or user-profile information; field masking is not documented. 6. Public endpoint rate limits are acknowledged without numeric values. maxTokenBudget truncates search results; fetch is not truncated by this option. No call prices or bulk caps are published. 7. Published tool parameters are query, url, and optional language. Runtime tool schemas may change. Validation/correction implementation is not public. 8. Logging, audit trail, and MCP telemetry behavior are not documented. 9. No feedback, rating, report, survey, or upsell tool appears in the complete official tool list. Docs invite feedback through the repository. 10. Server-side initialize instructions and skills are not published. Separate repository skills/plugins provide client-side guidance; official setup example recommends using the tools for narrowly defined Microsoft-technology questions. 11. No server memory behavior is documented. 12. Microsoft describes a hosted MCP server in front of the Learn knowledge service/vector store; it is one endpoint with a flat published tool list, not documented as MCP subservers. 13. No raw API, SQL, script execution, or other general escape-hatch tool appears in the official list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: When handling questions around how to work with native Microsoft technologies, such as C#, F#, ASP.NET Core, Microsoft.Extensions, NuGet, Entity Framework, the `dotnet` runtime - please use these tools for research purposes when dealing with specific / narrowly defined questions that may occur.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The hosted server exposes a flat set of three tools over Streamable HTTP. Microsoft says it fronts the Learn knowledge service; no MCP hierarchy or dynamically loaded toolsets are documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official developer reference lists three tools (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/support/mcp-developer-reference); the official repository README also names three and publishes parameter summaries. No official total beyond those three is stated. No catalogue-only tools were added. Claude's third-party connector directory lists the same three. integrations.sh has no tool-name list and its OAuth claim conflicts with Microsoft's unauthenticated documentation and the supplied 404 OAuth metadata.

actions.description: Performs semantic search against Microsoft official technical documentation.
Fetches and converts a Microsoft documentation page into Markdown.
Searches official Microsoft and Azure code snippets and examples.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server's complete tool definitions and initialize instructions are not publicly available. The public repository is a client/plugin/CLI and does not contain the hosted server code.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Microsoft Learn's broader site includes training and user-profile services, but Microsoft says the MCP endpoint contains publicly available documentation, not training or user-profile information. Product/account actions are not exposed by the three read-only MCP tools. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/support/mcp and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/termsofuse.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The developer reference says clients should call the tool list at initialization because tools may change. Best practices advise refreshing after 400/404 responses and using maxTokenBudget to limit search output. The get-started example recommends that agents use the tools for specific, narrowly defined Microsoft-technology questions; these are client instructions and are not documented as server-enforced.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Microsoft says access is unauthenticated and that the MCP service contains publicly available documentation rather than training or user-profile information. The Learn Terms of Use apply. The general Terms state that services are provided “AS IS”; no MCP-specific retention, logging, AI-training, or data-protection promises were found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Microsoft describes the service as providing trusted, up-to-date official documentation and code samples. It says the underlying knowledge service refreshes incrementally after content updates and fully refreshes daily.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Read-only retrieval matches the published tools. The documented update cadence and public-content scope describe the source service, but the implementation details are closed. Client recommendations to discover tools and steer agent use are not enforced server-side in the reviewed evidence.

contradictions: integrations.sh labels the endpoint as using OAuth and describes a standard OAuth flow, but Microsoft says authentication is not required; the supplied protected-resource and authorization-server metadata URLs returned HTTP 404. The catalogue appears inconsistent with official documentation and the prefetched endpoint evidence.

Microsoft's endpoint overview says content refreshes incrementally and receives a full daily refresh, while the FAQ says data changes whenever content is added, modified, or deleted, usually daily. These statements describe different update timing and cadence, without an explicit reconciliation.
observations_for_research: Microsoft describes runtime tool discovery as intentional because tool names, schemas, and behavior may evolve; its guidance tells clients to refresh tool lists after 400 or 404 errors.

The official setup instructions include client-side prompt guidance to prefer Learn tools for narrowly defined questions about native Microsoft technologies; the reviewed documentation does not say the server enforces that rule.
The official repository offers separate client-side skills and a CLI fallback, but those artifacts are not the hosted endpoint implementation.
notes: Checked the prepared pages, links.json, links_check.txt, OAuth evidence, and cloned repository at the recorded commit. The public repository is for a CLI/plugin/skills, not hosted-server code; its tool table is treated as official documentation, not deployed implementation. The official developer reference, repository README, engineering blog, and Claude listing agree on three tools. integrations.sh has a verified authentication inconsistency and was not used as tool evidence. The npm page returned HTTP 403. OAuth well-known responses were used as supplied; no OAuth values or scopes were published.
